auditFocus: async void used outside an event handler, swallowing any exception the method throws
a blocking `.Result`/`.Wait()` call on a Task from synchronous code, risking a sync-over-async deadlock
a public API returning a nullable-looking reference type with nullable annotations disabled, or an unannotated parameter that is dereferenced without a null check
IDisposable/IAsyncDisposable fields or locals not wrapped in `using`/`await using`, leaking unmanaged resources or connections
SQL built by string interpolation/concatenation into SqlCommand.CommandText instead of parameterized queries
a unit test mocking an internal collaborator (a private helper, a concrete implementation detail) instead of the external seam (HTTP client, repository interface, database)
fixGuardrails: never add `#pragma warning disable` or `[SuppressMessage]` to silence a compiler/analyzer warning without fixing or explaining the underlying issue
never downgrade or disable nullable reference types (`<Nullable>disable</Nullable>` or a blanket `#nullable disable`) just to make a nullability warning disappear
never pin or downgrade a NuGet package to route around a real incompatibility without saying so in the report
fix the smallest root cause; do not refactor unrelated code while resolving a build/test/analyzer failure
